segments.text: அரசியல் நோயாளிகள்

blocks.text: அரசியல் நோயாளிகள்

segments.text: கண்னை மூடிக்கொண்டே படுத்திருப்பார்கள். திடுக்கென கத்துவார்கள் 'அய்யோ அப்பா' என்று! இப்படி சில அரசியல் நோயாளிகள் இருக்கிறார்கள். நான் நோயாளி என்கிறேன்; அதை அவர்கள் 'ஸ்டண்ட்' என்பார்கள், வாயை மூடி வாலைச்சுருட்டி உட்கார்ந்திருப்பது. எதிர்பாராத நேரத்தில் எழுந்து பாய்வது. அந்தப் பாய்ச்சலிலே பயன் இருந்தால் மேலும் மேலும் தாவுவது, இல்லாவிட்டால் பழைய படியே மரக்கிளையில் தொங்குவது. இது நமது அக்கிரஹாரத்தின் பிரதிநிதி—அம்மாமிகளின் அபிமானச் செல்வன் ஆனந்தவிகடனுக்குப் பழக்கமான சமாச்சாரம்.

segments.text: Political Patients

blocks.text: Political Patients

segments.text: They lie there, eyes shut. Suddenly they cry out, 'Oh, father!' There are some political patients like this. I call them patients; they call it a 'stunt'—mouth shut, tail tucked in. Suddenly getting up and pouncing. If the pounce pays, they leap farther and farther; if not, they hang from the tree branch as before. This is a familiar affair for Ananda Vikatan, the representative of our agraharam—the beloved child of the ammamis.

blocks.text: Racial Hatred—Attachment to One's Race

segments.text: Racial hatred is indeed wrong. That is exactly what we keep pointing out to the Aryan race. We say: give up the arrogance that a human being must not be touched—the thick-headed conceit that you alone must worship Maheswaran—give up racial hatred. What we have is not racial hatred but attachment to our race. Racial hatred...destroying and suppressing another race and developing one's own. Attachment to one's race..protecting one's own race and creating a racial awakening.

segments.text: There stands that Iyer on Chennai's seashore. All who come and go look at him as they pass. He does wear the sacred thread. The thread is only hidden beneath his shirt—that is all. To those coming toward the beach, he says, "Countrymen; countrymen, a message." And he doesn't stop there. "There is a word called Dravidam; it is sweet-tasting honey, language sugar-candy," he sings. You will be astonished.

segments.text: An Ayyar accepting Dravidam? You will be startled. True, friends, true! One day, my friends and I met that Ayyar on the beach. He sang the song above. He cried, 'Dravidam, Dravidam'. Even one member of the "Enothano" party—one who, at the very word Dravidam, leaps as though he has stepped on fire—heard that Ayyar's cry and went away, head bowed.
